hero.lead: A nation of 51.4 million whose electricity is almost entirely renewable, that commissioned the 600 megawatt Karuma dam in 2024, and where nearly half of citizens are not yet connected.

capital.heading: 25 instruments. A railway from Malaba to Kampala, power to the last mile, and health, schools, farms and cities.

record.text: Total public debt stock at the end of June 2026, up from $32.30 billion a year earlier: domestic debt $20.82 billion and external debt $16.30 billion, 54.3% of GDP in nominal terms
Islamic Development Bank financing approved in June 2026 for the Malaba–Kampala Standard Gauge Railway, the largest amount its Board has approved for a single project in Uganda

United States health support of approximately $1.7 billion for 2026 to 2030, under a Strategic Objective Agreement signed in September 2026; the United States intends to channel it through government systems as budget support
Existing World Bank Group portfolio in Uganda, as the Group launched a ten-year strategy for 2026 to 2035 and anticipates an indicative lending programme of about $2 billion per IDA three-year cycle
Electricity Access Scale-up Project: IDA financing for the last mile, with 1,073,500 grid connections in the indicative investment plan

register.name: Karuma Hydropower Plant
register.detail: Commissioned 26 September 2024 · Built by Sinohydro
register.note: Financed 15% by the Government of Uganda and 85% by the Export-Import Bank of China
register.text: A 600 MW hydropower plant in Kiryandongo District, built by Sinohydro, which the chair of the Karuma and Isimba Hydropower Project Steering Committee called “Africa’s largest underground hydropower plant” at its commissioning. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: Uganda–Tanzania Interconnector Project (UTIP)
register.detail: Approved, announced 18 June 2026 · IDA · First phase of the $1.6 billion RETRADE-EA programme · About 260 km of 400 kV double-circuit line
register.note: 1,000 MW of transfer capacity between Uganda and Tanzania
register.text: A new high-voltage line from Wobulenzi to Masaka and Mutukula, on the border with Tanzania, that links Uganda to the regional grid so that surplus hydropower can be sold. The World Bank expects at least 452 gigawatt-hours a year to be traded between Uganda and Tanzania by 2031 (a projection). It serves the energy and livelihood standards.

register.name: Uganda Cities and Municipalities Infrastructure Development (UCMID)
register.detail: Approved, announced 31 March 2026 · IDA · Program-for-Results · Six years
register.note: 5.6 million people, among them 600,000 refugees
register.text: Results-based financing for climate-smart urban infrastructure in 10 cities, 26 municipalities and 13 refugee-hosting districts, succeeding the USMID programme that closed in 2024. At least 40,000 direct jobs are expected, 20,000 of them permanent. It serves the shelter and livelihood standards.

register.name: Strengthening Public Investment and Asset Management for Growth and Resilience (PIM Plus)
register.detail: Approved 3 September 2025 · IDA · Borrowing approved by Parliament 29 October 2025
register.note: Public investment and asset management
register.text: Strengthens government efficiency, accountability and the sustainability of public investment and asset management. It serves all seven standards through better public investment.

register.name: Uganda Learning Acceleration Program (ULEARN)
register.detail: Approved 4 June 2025 · IDA · Borrowing approved by Parliament 29 October 2025
register.note: Learning environments in target schools
register.text: Aims to improve learning environments in target schools. It serves the education standard, where 18.1% of children read a simple text by the end of primary school (World Bank, 2014).

register.name: Development Response to Displacement Impacts Project, Phase II (DRDIP II)
register.detail: Approved 4 June 2025 · IDA · Parliament approved borrowing of $180.5 million for it on 29 October 2025
register.note: Refugees and host communities
register.text: The second phase of the Development Response to Displacement Impacts Project, which seeks to expand economic opportunities for host communities and refugees. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Northern Uganda Social Action Fund IV (NUSAF IV)
register.detail: Approved 1 April 2025 · IDA · Five years · Borrowing approved by Parliament 29 October 2025
register.note: Over three million beneficiaries expected
register.text: The fourth Northern Uganda Social Action Fund, which strengthens adaptive social protection systems in sub-regions that include West Nile, Acholi, Lango, Teso and Karamoja. It serves the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Uganda Climate Smart Agricultural Transformation Project
register.detail: Approved 22 December 2022 · IDA credit $325 million and IDA grant $25 million · Investment Project Financing · Expected closing 31 December 2028
register.note: About 760,000 households, 3.9 million people, to benefit directly
register.text: Climate-smart agriculture for smallholder farmers in 69 districts, seven of them refugee-hosting, run by the Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Industry and Fisheries over six years. It serves the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Generating Growth Opportunities and Productivity for Women Enterprises (GROW)
register.detail: Approved 17 June 2022 · IDA grant, SDR 161.5 million · Investment Project Financing · Expected closing 31 December 2027
register.note: Women’s businesses, including refugees and women in host communities
register.text: Finance and business support for women entrepreneurs, including refugees and women entrepreneurs from host communities. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Greater Kampala Metropolitan Area Urban Development Program
register.detail: Approved 31 May 2022 · IDA credit $518 million and IDA grant $48 million · Program-for-Results · Closing 31 December 2027 · Borrowing approved by Parliament 23 August 2023
register.note: With $571.31 million of counterpart funding, a $1.14 billion programme
register.text: Results-based financing for roads, infrastructure and services in Kampala and eight surrounding local governments, through the Ministry for Kampala Capital City and Metropolitan Affairs. It serves the shelter and livelihood standards.

register.name: Electricity Access Scale-up Project (EASP)
register.detail: Approved 31 March 2022 · IDA credit $331.5 million and IDA grant $236.5 million · Expected closing 30 June 2027
register.note: Plus $30 million from the Clean Technology Fund and $10 million from ESMAP; total financing $638 million
register.text: IDA financing for last-mile grid connections, with 1,073,500 connections in the indicative investment plan. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: Extended Credit Facility
register.detail: Approved 28 June 2021 · SDR 722 million, 200 percent of quota · Fifth review completed 6 March 2024 · “the expiration of the 2021–24 Extended Credit Facility arrangement” (IMF, July 2026)
register.note: About $870 million (SDR 631.75 million) disbursed by March 2024
register.text: IMF lending of about $1 billion under the 2021–24 arrangement, of which about $870 million was disbursed by March 2024. Since the arrangement expired, the IMF Executive Board has concluded a Post-Financing Assessment, on 12 January 2026, and the 2026 Article IV consultation, in July 2026.

register.name: Uganda Secondary Education Expansion Project
register.detail: Approved 23 July 2020 · IDA credit $90 million and IDA grant $60 million
register.note: Lower secondary schooling for underserved areas
register.text: Enhances access to lower secondary education, focusing on underserved populations in targeted areas. It serves the education standard.

register.name: Irrigation for Climate Resilience Project
register.detail: Approved 18 June 2020 · IDA credit, SDR 122.9 million · Investment Project Financing · Expected closing at appraisal 30 April 2026
register.note: 63,200 farmers as primary beneficiaries
register.text: Gives farmers in the project areas access to irrigation and other agricultural services. It serves the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Integrated Water Management and Development Project
register.detail: Approved 14 June 2018 · IDA credit $251 million and IDA grant $29 million at approval · Revised closing date of 31 January 2026 proposed in a 2024 restructuring paper
register.note: Total commitment in the World Bank Group’s 2026 portfolio snapshot; $280 million at approval, with $25 million of parallel KfW financing
register.text: Water supply and sanitation services, integrated water resources management and the operational performance of service providers, including new coverage for refugees and host communities. It serves the water and shelter standards.

register.name: Uganda Airports Development Programme, Phase 1: Arua Airport
register.detail: Approved, announced 18 June 2026 · AfDB loan €141.15 million and ADF loan €14.84 million · Total cost €157.76 million
register.note: A 3.5-kilometre runway able to take a Boeing 777
register.text: African Development Bank Group financing to upgrade Arua Airport, with a 3.5-kilometre paved runway, a passenger terminal for 700,000 travellers a year and a cargo terminal for 25,000 tonnes a year. It serves the livelihood standard through regional trade and tourism.

register.name: Standard Gauge Railway (Malaba–Kampala) Project
register.detail: Approved June 2026 by the 367th meeting of the IsDB Board of Executive Directors, Baku · Release of 16 June 2026 · Financial close targeted by the Government for November 2026
register.note: The largest amount the IsDB Board has approved for a single project in Uganda, according to the Ministry of Finance
register.text: Islamic Development Bank financing to build the Malaba–Kampala standard gauge railway, including, according to the Ministry of Finance, the 553-metre Jinja Nile Bridge, the 2.12-kilometre Mbuya–Kampala tunnel, six stations and three workshops. The IsDB expects lower transport costs and travel times and about 3,000 jobs; it serves the livelihood and food standards.

register.name: Uganda Multipurpose Water for Climate Resilient Irrigation Development and Agro-Industrialization Programme
register.detail: Approved, announced 12 June 2026 · African Development Fund loan · Total cost $207 million, with the OPEC Fund, the Government of Uganda and others
register.note: More than 4,000 hectares at first, with potential to reach 13,000
register.text: An African Development Fund loan for water-transfer infrastructure and irrigation networks, expected to create more than 13,000 direct jobs and reach more than 121,000 households directly, and about 21,000 schoolchildren through school feeding. It serves the food, water and livelihood standards.

register.name: Uganda Rural Electricity Access Project (UREAP), Phases I and II
register.detail: Approved 7 April 2026 · €7.33 million additional financing for Phase I · Phase II AfDB loan €86.58 million, with a €12.93 million loan and a €1.72 million grant from the Climate Investment Funds · Phase II total cost €104.39 million
register.note: 259,723 new grid and mini-grid connections over six years in Phase II
register.text: Phase II builds about 624 km of medium-voltage and 2,154 km of low-voltage lines to give first-time electricity to nearly 1.18 million people, including more than 250,000 households and 3,000 businesses; the Phase I top-up completes compensation and outstanding works. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: Busega–Mpigi Expressway, additional financing (Multinational Busega–Mpigi and Kagitumba–Kayonza–Rusumo Roads Project)
register.detail: Approved, announced 6 November 2025 · ADB loan €188.18 million, ADF loan €28.31 million and a $1 million NEPAD-IPPF grant · Government of Uganda €30.98 million
register.note: Uganda section now costed at €424.61 million, from €176.26 million
register.text: Completes the 27.3-kilometre Busega–Mpigi expressway on the Northern Corridor from Kampala to Kigali, with interchanges, seven new bridges, toll plazas and 54 km of lined drainage. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Uganda Biogas and Electric Cooking Project
register.detail: Approved, announced 7 May 2025 · Mainly from the African Development Fund’s Climate Action Window, 64% of the cost · Co-funded by the UK FCDO and the Government of Uganda
register.note: About 77,000 electric cooking devices and 47 biogas plants
register.text: Builds 47 biogas plants for schools, markets and farming communities and provides about 77,000 affordable electric cooking devices in major urban centres, with standards, repair services and distribution for the appliances. It reaches clean cooking, which sets Uganda’s Coverage: 2% of Ugandans cook with clean fuels and technology.
by: UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office

register.name: Uganda–South Sudan Electricity Interconnection Project
register.detail: Approved 13 December 2024 by the ADF Board · ADF loan to Uganda · 299 km, 150 km of it in Uganda · Total cost $260 million
register.note: Part of $153.66 million from the ADF, with a $32.5 million grant to South Sudan
register.text: An electricity interconnection from Gumbo, near Juba, to Olwiyo, with new 400/132/33 kV substations at Gumbo and at Biba on the border, and upgrades at the Karuma and Olwiyo substations. It links the grids of Uganda and South Sudan and serves the energy and livelihood standards.

register.name: United States–Uganda health cooperation: Strategic Objective Agreement
register.detail: Signed, announced 8 September 2026 · Implements the bilateral health MOU of 10 December 2025 · 2026 to 2030 · The United States intends to channel the support through government systems as budget support
register.note: About Shs 6.42 trillion; under the MOU, Uganda pledges to raise its own health spending by $577 million
register.text: United States support of approximately $1.7 billion for the prevention, detection and response to emerging and existing infectious disease threats, in a shift from mostly off-budget assistance to government-to-government financing. The MOU’s priorities are outbreak response, reducing the burden of disease, strengthening frontline workers and data digitisation for accountability; it serves the health standard.

register.name: Project for the Reconstruction of Karuma Bridge
register.detail: Grant agreement signed 25 March 2025, Kampala · Japanese grant aid · 60 months, including detailed design and bidding · Executing agency: Ministry of Works and Transport
register.note: JPY 4,939 million
register.text: A JICA grant to rebuild the Karuma Bridge and its approach road on the main road between Kiryandongo and Nwoya districts, improving traffic flow and road safety on the northern corridor. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Support Rural Livelihoods Uganda, loan for MSMEs (Stanbic Bank Uganda)
register.detail: Approved 15 May 2025 · Signed 31 July 2025 in two tranches of €25 million and €75 million · Credit facility for on-lending
register.note: €80 million for agricultural projects and €20 million for women borrowers
register.text: A European Investment Bank credit facility to Stanbic Bank Uganda for on-lending to micro, small and medium-sized enterprises and mid-caps, focused on sustainable agriculture, food security and women’s economic empowerment, jointly with the Gates Foundation. It serves the food and livelihood standards.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Nile
items.label: Karuma hydropower, commissioned September 2024
items.text: Financed 15% by the government and 85% by the Export-Import Bank of China.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewables, 2023
items.alt: Power lines across the Ugandan countryside

items.name: The Land
items.label: Of land in agriculture, 2024
items.text: Coffee, bananas and maize across four-fifths of the country.
items.alt: Coffee and banana farms in Uganda

items.name: The Ground
items.label: Natural resource rents, share of GDP, 2021
items.text: Oil under development in the Albertine Rift, and minerals.
items.alt: The Albertine Rift near Lake Albert

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: One of the youngest populations on Earth. Remittances equal 4.5% of GDP.

items.name: Pearl Dairy
items.text: Established in Uganda in 2009, it makes UHT and powder milks, flavoured milks, yoghurts, butter and honey. In 2023 IFC approved up to $8.75 million, a concessional subordinated loan under the GAFSP Private Sector Window, alongside a loan package of up to $35 million from IFC and FMO, for capacity expansion that includes its powder milk plant in Uganda.

items.name: Water Mission Uganda
items.text: Has worked in Uganda since 2007 and serves nearly 1.1 million people through community-based piped water systems, emergency water treatment, latrines, handwashing stations and school washrooms. It works with UNHCR in refugee settlements, in the West Nile (Yumbe, Terego, Madi Okolo) and in the East Nile (Luuka, Buyende).

items.name: Housing Finance Bank
items.text: A partner of AFD since 2011, it rolls out housing microfinance through its 19 branches across Uganda. In 2020 it signed a €10 million AFD line of credit to deploy its housing microfinance and affordable housing offer to low- and middle-income households who do not have access to an adequate financial offer.

items.name: Fenix International, an ENGIE company
items.text: Sells solar home systems in Uganda under pay-as-you-go contracts. In 2020 the EIB lent it $12.5 million to roll out 240,000 solar home systems, so that over a million people across Uganda could have electricity for the first time.

items.name: Educate!
items.text: Launched its flagship in-school model, the Educate! Experience, in Uganda in 2009. It gives secondary students leadership, entrepreneurship and workforce readiness training, with mentorship, to start real businesses at school.

items.name: Living Goods
items.text: Began its community health programme in Uganda in 2007 and supports over 2,400 community health workers, known locally as Village Health Teams, reaching 1.4 million Ugandans with essential health care. The Ministry of Health chose it to lead the digital eCHIS rollout in six districts, completed in late 2023.

items.name: Centenary Bank
items.text: Lends to micro-enterprises under a €50 million EIB Global credit line, part of a €100 million programme signed in 2024. In the first year more than 24,000 micro-enterprises received financing, over 60% of the beneficiaries were women and 75% of the projects were in rural areas.
